gen-silkscreen-gf-assistant: Assistant keeps its mouths open on c, e and a, a quiet contemporary voice under the heading. Silkscreen is the one that grabs, its horizontals as heavy as its verticals, and Assistant is the one that lets you read on.
gen-silkscreen-gf-asta-sans: Asta Sans draws tubelike lines with no fuss. Silkscreen brings the retro, lo-fi spark in its spaced-out letters, while the body stays friendly and unmistakable, and that handoff is what makes the pair work.
gen-silkscreen-gf-bai-jamjuree: Light, unpinched round letters make Bai Jamjuree feel approachable. Silkscreen's pixel-spaced display letters sit on top with a retro grin, and the plain sans underneath keeps its stroke the same all the way through.
gen-silkscreen-gf-barlow: Silkscreen spaces its letters out with a lo-fi, retro swagger that you can almost feel around each one. But Barlow does the quieter work, pulling the tips of its c shapes well apart in neon-tube strokes of constant width.
gen-silkscreen-gf-biz-udgothic: BIZ UDGothic reads modern and businesslike, with a wide channel leading into every bowl. Silkscreen looks like bent paperclip wire beside it, while BIZ UDGothic would carry a long page of text in a steady, open way.
gen-silkscreen-gf-biz-udpgothic: Silkscreen has a pen-plotter smoothness, with lo-fi, retro letters that hold a lot of space around them. BIZ UDPGothic matches that generosity with lavish spacing.
gen-silkscreen-gf-bpmf-huninn: Bpmf Huninn reads modern and outline-like, with a single weight and a wide channel into every bowl of the sans. Silkscreen handles the retro showmanship, and Huninn handles the reading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-bpmf-zihi-kai-std: Retro and lo-fi up top, then gentler below: Silkscreen draws every stroke at one weight, while Bpmf Zihi Kai Std swells just a little in its curves like thread against yarn. A long passage would feel connected and easy.
gen-silkscreen-gf-cairo: Cairo opens its bowls wide, with a modern, businesslike feel, under a heading whose curves never thin at the turns. Give Cairo a bit more size than you might expect.
gen-silkscreen-gf-cairo-play: Cairo Play has open round letters that stay clear at small sizes, modern and tidy. Silkscreen does best with its drawn-with-one-tip simplicity and retro, lo-fi charm, while Cairo Play does best at carrying the actual reading.
